quotes.speaker: Brandin Podziemski
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandin Podziemski on the necessity of stepping back to regain balance
quotes.excerpt: The only way you can catch yourself is by moving backward away from the rim.
quotes.quote: When you get here, the only way you can get balance again is by going backwards. You land like this, the only way you can catch yourself is by moving backward away from the rim, which is why the coach always talks about you running away from your shot. It's really because we're like this, so you have to naturally take that backward step or steps to be able to get on balance again.

quotes.speaker: Travis Walton
quotes.summary_phrase: Travis Walton on the importance of staying vertical for shooting consistency
quotes.excerpt: When you stick it and you're as vertical as you can be, your consistency is going to be that much higher.
quotes.quote: It's still in sight. Get outside it. Get outside that ball they're going this way here which is in that pocket and just stick it and stay. When you stick it and you're as vertical as you can be, and you stay with the shot and you hold that finish old school, your consistency is going to be that much higher. That 3 to 5 percent, we're chasing 15 more makes in a season.

quotes.speaker: Brandin Podziemski
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandin Podziemski on the connection between shoulder position and shooting form
quotes.excerpt: You start to lose that crease, and then what happens? Now we're losing our shoulder.
quotes.quote: I understand, I believe in the shoulder, but when we say shoulder it's not this part of the shoulder, it's this part of the shoulder. Same thing with that crease. You start to lose that crease, and then what happens? Now we're losing our shoulder, the part that we actually want to be shooting from. Everything is connected. We lose this, we lose this, I'm shooting here and it's going outside, versus maintaining that crease which will maintain this crease, which is going to maintain the follow-through.
